Quasi-degenerate cation occupation enables oxygen-vacancy defect healing in nonlinear optical crystals
articles.abstract: Abstract Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which couple with dopants and obscure or degrade the intrinsic properties. Therefore, chemical substitution that enables atomically precise engineering of materials without generating defect structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to overcome this detrimental coupling and successfully apply it to the langasite-family nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal, La 3 TiGa 5 O 14 (LGTi). Therein, the cross-site occupation of Ti and Ti 3+ /Ti 4+ redox flexibility improves the kinetic accessibility of oxygen-vacancy ( V O ) defects associated with cation disorder, enabling their removal during oxidative annealing. The oxidized LGTi single crystal has a V O -related defect concentration below the electron paramagnetic resonance detection limit, with a laser damage threshold of 2.53 GW/cm 2 and a large NLO coefficient of 3.51 pm/V, both exceeding the previously reported values for bulk langasite-family crystals. Overall, this work provides a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to mitigate substitution-induced defects in structurally complex crystalline systems and has great prospects in enhancing material performance.

articles.title:
Climate Effect of
Alternative Binders: Life Cycle
Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Potential as a Carbon Sink
articles.abstract: Abstract Substituting Portland cement (PC) with alternative binders offers a promising pathway to mitigate the climate impacts of the cement industry, one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonize. While substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are generated during production, most alternative binders can sequester CO2 during their service life. This effect has been acknowledged from a technical perspective, yet its significant influences on the GHG footprint of alternative binders remain unresolved. In this study, we quantify the CO2 uptake of common alternative binders alongside their lifetime GHG emissions. We demonstrate that most binders can take up a larger amount of CO2 than PC during usage, due to a thermodynamically high uptake capacity or high uptake kinetics. The uptake reactions enable a dynamic CO2 loop, with 1–248% of the production emissions being recovered over a 100-year structure service life. However, when the slow reaction rate is considered, the associated climate benefits can be up to 71% lower than the theoretical apparent uptake value. Our results highlight the importance of combined CO2 uptake modeling in assessing the decarbonization potential of alternative binders, and provide a basis for justifying the capability of these binders for use as building carbon sinks.

articles.title:
From
Bulk Removal
to Precision: The Next 60 Years
of Water Treatment

Reconciliation
through Integration: A Source-Level
Bayesian Framework for Developing Measurement-Integrated Methane Inventories
articles.abstract: Abstract Bottom-up (BU) inventories and top-down (TD) aerial measurements at midstream natural gas facilities frequently diverge, and this discrepancy remains a central challenge for methane accounting in the sector. Previous approaches typically reconcile this divergence by treating BU and TD data as independent estimates of a single true quantity to be adjusted toward agreement, rather than as evidence that each captures only part of a more complex underlying system. This complexity arises from methane emissions being strongly governed by equipment operational state and therefore instantaneous aerial “snapshots” translate poorly to annual inventories. We argue instead that BU and TD are complementary sources of evidence that should be integrated. We present a source-level Bayesian framework that constructs BU prior distributions for each emission source category and updates them with attributed aerial detections through an empirical data-augmentation procedure. The resulting posterior distributions were propagated through unit-level activity data and source-specific information via Monte Carlo simulation to produce annual estimates. Across 64 compressor stations, measurement-integrated annual estimates were 84% higher than the BU inventory, a difference driven almost entirely by compressor vents (rod packing and seal vents) and leakage through blowdown and isolation valves, which together accounted for 90% of the asset-level revision. The revision was heterogeneous across stations and source categories, emphasizing the importance of source-level, station-specific integration when developing an emissions inventory.

articles.title:
Uranium(VI)
Removal from Water by Continuous-Flow
Iron Electrocoagulation: Removal Pathways and Uranium Retention in
Residual Solids
articles.abstract: Abstract The removal of uranium(VI) from groundwater is important for both drinking water treatment and pump-and-treat remediation of contaminated aquifers. This study evaluated U(VI) removal by continuous flow-through iron electrocoagulation (EC) under realistic treatment conditions and environmentally relevant water chemistries. The effects of iron dose, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), dissolved inorganic carbon, and Ca2+ were examined using EC followed by flocculation and sedimentation. Under oxic conditions, U(VI) was removed by adsorption to EC-generated Fe(III) oxides. Under anoxic conditions, U(VI) was removed via a two-step pathway of adsorption followed by reduction to less soluble U(IV) and U(V) species by mixed-valent iron solids (green rust and magnetite). Among the tested combinations of pH (6–8) and DO (oxic and anoxic), the best overall U(VI) removal performance was achieved under oxic pH 7 and anoxic pH 8 conditions. Both conditions gave effective (>90%) removal after 11 s of residence time in the EC reactor, followed by up to 10 min of post-EC treatment with a 10 mg/L Fe dose. Carbonate species and Ca2+ inhibited removal under both oxic and anoxic conditions by forming stable aqueous complexes with U(VI). EC achieved faster and greater U(VI) removal than with chemical coagulation or contact with preformed iron solids. The stability of U removed during anoxic EC was evaluated by exposing residual solids to air. After 24 h of air exposure, only ∼10% of U was released to water. The majority of immobilized U likely remained associated with magnetite. This study provides mechanistic insight into U(VI) removal, solid reactivity, and U stability during EC.

articles.title: Heparan sulfate sulfatases are essential for the patterning of human stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons
articles.abstract: Abstract Midbrain dopaminergic neurons (mDA) are selectively lost in Parkinson’s disease, driving sustained efforts to generate bona fide mDA neurons from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) for replacement therapy. While morphogen gradients and transcription factors have been extensively studied, extracellular regulators remain largely overlooked. Here, we identify the heparan sulfate-modifying enzymes SULF1 and SULF2 as essential for establishing mDA neuron identity in vitro. Using CRISPR/Cas9-engineered iPSCs, we show that loss of SULF1/2 increases 6-O-sulfated heparan sulfate species and disrupts patterning both at the anteroposterior and dorsoventral axes in human iPSC-derived mDA cultures. Double-knockout cells thus fail to acquire ventral midbrain fates and instead adopt hindbrain, spinal cord and neural crest-like identities as revealed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Mechanistically, we partially explain the changed patterning to aberrant FGF signaling and demonstrate that FGF inhibition redirects cells toward midbrain fates, however without restoring ventral identity. These findings establish a critical role for SULF1/2 in mDA neuron in vitro differentiation and uncover a previously unrecognized layer of extracellular control over neural patterning.

articles.title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
articles.abstract: Abstract Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. Using 259,732 phenological observations across eight European woody species spanning 1950–2024, we show that foliar frost damage shortened the fruit development period (FDP; the interval from flowering to fruit maturity) by 1.6 days, driven by delayed flowering and advanced fruit maturity. Conversely, floral frost damage prolonged FDP by 1.3 days through delayed fruit maturity, with both effects strengthening under greater frost severity. Accounting for anomalously warm conditions in the frost year substantially reduced the estimated delays in flowering and subsequent-year phenology, indicating that neglecting climatic context leads to overestimation of frost effects. These findings reveal organ-specific pathways through which frost damage reshapes reproductive phenology while generating limited carry-over effects, refining current understanding of phenological responses under climate change.

articles.title: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
articles.abstract: Abstract Stature is a key indicator of pediatric health, yet the molecular and metabolic architecture governing childhood growth remains incompletely defined. We conduct genome-wide association analyses of stature from birth to childhood (574,580 measurements; 72,704 Norwegian children) and integrate UK Biobank data (age 10 and adulthood). We uncover life-stage shifts in the genetics of stature, identifying previously not identified childhood-specific effects including variants near GLP1R with BMI-independent effects, and reveal three temporal clusters - Infancy and Childhood clusters enriched for endocrine and metabolic pathways, and a Lifetime growth cluster enriched for skeletal biology. Proteome analysis reveals that prepubertal height is associated with widespread changes in the circulation, identifying 106 height-associated proteins and linking IGF1, IGF2, and IGFBP3 levels to childhood-height polygenic scores. Mendelian randomization shows that reduced fetal growth and taller prepubertal height increase type 2 diabetes risk, independent of adult stature. These findings uncover developmental stage-specific genetic and proteomic influences on child-growth and links to adult metabolic health.

articles.title: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events
articles.abstract: Abstract How do our brains manage to store our everyday experiences into memory? Neurons in the human temporal lobe that respond to the concept of an individual person or object have been shown to provide the semantic building blocks for episodic memory. Recording from 1415 neurons in neurosurgical patients who learned a story involving specific concepts, we found reactivation of neurons representing these concepts during slow-wave sleep after learning. Concept neurons were conjointly reactivated, particularly during sharp-wave ripples, with time lags suitable for synaptic modification. However, the temporal sequence of reactivation did not reflect the sequence of concepts in the learned story. Unlike rodent place cells, which can acquire preferred firing locations during exploration of new environments according to their pre-existing preferred sequence of activation, human concept neurons are tuned to specific semantic contents before learning starts. Consequently, pre-existing firing sequences correlate with consecutive place fields in rodents, but not with sequences of events in human experience. Thus, in contrast to reactivation of rodent place cells, reactivation of human concept cells does not reflect sequences of events in human experience.

articles.title: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
articles.abstract: Abstract Benzoxaboroles (BoBs) such as acoziborole feature a boron-heterocyclic core and are an important innovation in the development of drugs against a range of pathogens and other pathologies. A broad pharmacological spectrum is associated with chemically diverse BoB derivatives, including multiple modes-of-action (MoA) and molecular targets. However, a consensus MoA for BoBs targeting evolutionarily diverse protozoan pathogens has emerged, with identification of CPSF3 in the CPSF complex as a target in both apicomplexan and kinetoplastida parasites. Here, using comprehensive genetic screens in Trypanosoma brucei , we establish a functional connection between the boron-heterocyclic scaffold shared by all BoBs and protein sumoylation genes. We observe a rapid, transient increase in global protein sumoylation following BoB exposure. While we do not observe direct CPSF3 sumoylation, we find that acoziborole and other BoBs rapidly and specifically destabilise CPSF3 in a SUMO- and proteasome-dependent manner.

Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
articles.abstract: Abstract Although desmin intermediate filaments are critical for muscle architecture and homeostasis, their spatial 3D organization remains elusive. Their known localization to sarcomeric Z-lines delimits the periodic array of actin and myosin filaments. Here, using d STORM and SIM sub-diffraction resolution microscopy, we resolve the spatial 3D organization of desmin filaments within mouse skeletal muscle, and reveal they are not confined to Z-lines. Our reconstruction reveals that desmin intermediate filaments extend from Z-lines into the sarcomere interior, where they align with actin filaments. Functional assays show that disrupting desmin filament assembly in normal male mouse muscle using a dominant negative inhibitor of desmin selectively reduces active tension at longer sarcomere lengths, indicating a role for desmin in sarcomere mechanics. These findings expand the structural model of the muscle sarcomere and support a role for desmin in force production.

articles.title: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
articles.abstract: Abstract The auditory brainstem implant (ABI) targeting the cochlear nucleus (CN) can restore hearing in patients ineligible for cochlear implants. However, conventional ABI using surface electrode array yields highly variable outcomes, from poor to moderate, due to limited spatial resolution and restricted tonotopic access. Here, we developed a penetrating ABI based on a high-density, ultra-flexible implantable neural electrode array (uFINE). In normal-hearing rats, uFINE mapped frequency tuning from 0.5 to 32 kHz in CN and the inferior colliculus (IC). Selective CN stimulation via uFINE evoked IC responses closely matching acoustic tonotopy, with IC tuning widths comparable to tone-evoked responses, and these remained stable for over 136 days, with minimal gliosis observed. Daily sequential CN–IC microstimulation progressively shifted the location of the CN-evoked IC response peak toward the targeted IC stimulation site, consistent with use-dependent plasticity. Together, these findings demonstrate that uFINE enables high-resolution, tonotopically precise, and long-term stable CN stimulation across a broad frequency range with minimal tissue disruption, highlighting its potential to enhance ABI-mediated hearing restoration.

articles.title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors

Human Mitochondrial
HVRII as an Indicator of Island
Groundwater Connectivity
articles.abstract: Abstract This study explores the use of human mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) as a potential tracer for anthropogenic inputs in confined groundwater systems, building on our previous application in urban watersheds. mtDNA represents one of the most robust sources of eukaryotic environmental DNA (eDNA) due to its multimembrane protection, high copy number per cell, and persistence in the environment, resulting in a valuable resource for both detection and when examining sequences, tracing. We investigated mtDNA transport in the groundwater of Lord Howe Island, a small shield volcano remnant and UNESCO World Heritage site, whose modest population and limited tourist load yield a tractable number of haplotypes. By targeting the hypervariable region II (HVRII) of the human mitochondrial genome, we examined the impact of local human inputs, including septic tanks, on local groundwater. Groundwater samples were collected from wells and small groundwater discharges, PCR-amplified, and analyzed via high-throughput sequencing, revealing unique haplotype frequencies that identified zones of impact. These findings were supported by Bacteroides 16S tracking, using human, bovine, and canine specific markers as well as bacterial counts and other water quality parameters. This approach demonstrates several advantages over more traditional source tracking markers, most importantly, which impacts are uniquely anthropogenic and their origin. Unlike artificial DNA tracers, mtDNA is naturally present in septic tank leach fields and is temporally unambiguous, like plant-based viral markers. Our work highlights mtDNA’s potential to help map anthropogenic inputs within groundwater, which is a tool that may be particularly valuable for island communities with limited wastewater infrastructure resources.

articles.title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
articles.abstract: Abstract In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC + ), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC + with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC + participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC + exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

articles.title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
articles.abstract: Abstract Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Here, we synthesized 276 studies and applied multilevel meta-analysis to paired LULCC comparisons. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. Pooled sustained-flux global warming potential (SGWP) was ‒122.41 ± 81.99 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 for natural coastal wetlands and 250.60 ± 101.06 for LULCC sites, corresponding to 0.17 ± 0.06 Gt CO 2 e of cumulative emissions over two decades. The descriptive SGWP contrast with pooled LULCC sites was larger for vegetated wetlands ( + 309.32%) than for tidal flats ( + 165.02%). Ecologically restored wetlands showed negative pooled SGWP ( − 33.03 ± 114.70 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 ), contrasting with the positive pooled LULCC estimate. Our results indicate that GHG responses to coastal wetland conversion are ecosystem- and pathway-specific, underscoring the importance of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
articles.abstract: Abstract Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) light is a central tool in modern photon science, probing the electronic, chemical and structural properties of matter. High-harmonic generation can extend the reach of laser sources into this spectral range, but the achievable photon flux falls sharply as photon energy increases. We show experimentally and theoretically that plasma-core-induced self-guiding of a visible-wavelength driver in helium sustains high intensity and favorable phase matching over an extended propagation length. We achieve a conversion efficiency of up to 10 −6 in a single high-harmonic line and phase-matched emission extending to 100 eV. With less than 10 W of average power at 516 nm from a frequency-doubled ytterbium laser, we generate 1.8 × 10 11 photons s −1 within 2 % bandwidth at 13.5 nm (91.8 eV), exceeding previous reports by more than an order of magnitude. These results establish a power-scalable XUV platform for actinic metrology, spectroscopy and coherent imaging.

Comprehensive Plant
Biomarker Profile for Tracing
Detection of Sulfur Mustard and Lewisite Exposure and Its Application
to Japanese Abandoned Chemical Weapon Samples
articles.abstract: Abstract Sulfur mustard (HD) and lewisite (L, mainly containing L1 and L2) from Japanese Abandoned Chemical Weapons (JACWs) in China have persisted for nearly a century, posing ongoing risks to ecological environments and public health. Plants can serve as monitoring sentinels for tracing detection of chemical exposure. However, specific plant biomarkers for HD/L remain unidentified, and their transformation in plants remains unveiled. By nontargeted metabolomics and high-resolution mass spectrometry, 30 novel plant adducts of HD/L were identified. Twelve of these adducts, along with 5 degradation products, were evaluated and assembled into a plant biomarker profile for retrospective detection of HD/L exposure. A sensitive UHPLC–TQ MS method was developed with LODs as low as 0.0200 ng/mL. The profile was detectable in 12 plant species for at least 90 days after exposure. Adduction, hydrolysis, oxidation, and trimerization of HD/L agents have been detected in plants, and transformation diagrams were portrayed. Real samples from JACW remediation sites in northeastern China were analyzed, and free biomarkers were detected at obviously higher levels in plants than in soil. Analytical results indicate that plant leaves may serve as sensitive monitoring media for the exposed agents. This work provides a reliable approach for long-term monitoring of JACW exposure and shows that possible plant accumulation and soil-to-plant transport of CWA products are valuable for further study.

articles.title:
Revisiting
the Characteristics and Performance of
Acid-Treated Polyamide Membranes: Fundamental Insights and Implications
articles.abstract: Abstract Acid treatment of polyamide reverse osmosis (RO) and nanofiltration (NF) membranes is a commonly used approach for membrane cleaning and modification. However, there are contradictory observations on the effects of acid treatment in the current literature. Herein, we systematically characterized the changes in the physicochemical properties of both RO and NF membranes under different acid treatment conditions. Both acid-treated RO and NF membranes exhibited similar surface physicochemical characteristics compared with their respective original membranes. Interestingly, the acid-treated RO membrane showed a nearly doubled water permeance while maintaining high salt rejection. During the acid treatment, the fully aromatic RO membrane underwent selective removal of monomers/oligomers from the bottom region of its asymmetric polyamide layer, as evidenced by the appearance of N-rich molecules in the acid rinsing solution and the increased O/N ratio of the polyamide bottom side. At the same time, the O/N ratio of the polyamide top surface was not affected. In comparison, no release of monomers/oligomers was detected during the acid treatment of the semiaromatic NF membrane. Correspondingly, the NF membrane had a comparable water permeance before and after acid treatment. In the current study, the acid-treated RO membrane demonstrated improved water permeance and stable rejection of NaCl and several micropollutants, suggesting that acid treatment could be used as a polishing strategy to improve the performance of RO membranes for high-efficiency water treatment.

articles.title:
Product
Formation
Dynamics and Sustainability in Chain
Elongation Systems: A Cross-Study Analysis
articles.abstract: Abstract As a promising strategy for sustainable resource recovery under the global energy crisis, chain elongation in anaerobic fermentation systems has attracted increasing attention. However, its optimization is constrained by limited understanding of dynamic behavior and its role in system-level decision-making. Here, we present a data-driven framework that progressively links dynamic process interpretation with predictive modeling and sustainability-oriented evaluation across heterogeneous chain elongation systems. Literature-derived time-series data were first analyzed to characterize product formation kinetics and identify mode-dependent relationships between process evolution and C6 formation. Building on these mechanistic insights, a random forest model using only initial operating conditions was developed to predict key kinetic descriptors, enabling pre-experimental screening of expected process behavior, while a hybrid dynamic model translated kinetic descriptors into complete product formation trajectories. Environmental and economic assessments further revealed substantial trade-offs among cost, product value, and environmental impact, with only 11 of 893 configurations (1.23%) identified as three-objective Pareto-efficient. Overall, this work provides a data-driven basis for identifying process-control priorities, screening operating conditions before extensive experimentation, anticipating product formation dynamics, and selecting configurations against multiple sustainability objectives.

articles.title:
Oxygen
Vacancies
in Metal-Based Catalysts for Advanced
Oxidation Processes: From Defect States to Reaction Pathways
articles.abstract: Abstract Oxygen vacancies (Vo) engineering can regulate oxidant adsorption and interfacial electron transfer in metal-based catalysts for advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), thereby overcoming inefficient oxidant activation, sluggish charge transfer, and limited pathway selectivity. Despite rapid advances in Vo synthesis, characterization, and catalytic applications, a unified understanding of how Vo govern the catalytic process remains lacking. This Review first summarizes the construction, classification, physicochemical properties, and characterization of Vo, followed by a critical evaluation of their identification as catalytically active sites. We then elucidate how Vo regulate the adsorption, activation, and transformation of oxidants and reactants, thereby governing both reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidation and electron-transfer processes (ETPs). Particular emphasis is placed on the emerging synergistic interactions between Vo and neighboring active sites, including metal centers, other vacancy defects, and heterojunction interfaces. More importantly, a unified framework is proposed to rationalize the divergent reaction pathways induced by Vo from the perspectives of catalyst–oxidant interactions, Vo concentration, and Vo type. These factors collectively determine local electronic structures, interfacial charge-transfer behaviors, and spin-state evolution, ultimately dictating the pathway selection between ROS generation and ETP. Finally, key challenges in Vo engineering, active-site identification, and pathway discrimination are highlighted together with future opportunities for advancing Vo-mediated AOPs. By shifting the focus from Vo generation to Vo-state regulation, this Review provides guidance for designing next-generation AOP catalysts with tunable reactivity, pathway selectivity, and long-term stability.

articles.title:
Interfacial
Water
Hydrogen-Bond Network Reorientation
Accelerates Advanced Oxidation for Micropollutant Abatement
articles.abstract: Abstract Interfacial water rigid hydrogen-bond (HB) networks impose significant thermodynamic and mass-transfer barriers in heterogeneous advanced oxidation processes. Herein, we propose a decoupled interfacial water oxidation process (decoupled interfacial oxidation process (DIOP)) strategy that dynamically reorganizes interfacial water to achieve pronounced kinetic acceleration and high decontamination selectivity. Localized electronic polarization drives cooperative reorientation of interfacial H2O, transforming rigid ice-like water clusters into a dynamic zigzag-like HB configuration. This structural relaxation significantly reduces interfacial solvent reorganization energy, shortens electron tunneling distances, and generates angstrom-scale dynamic low-density water microregions. These fluidic microregions selectively enrich small-molecule pollutants over bulky natural organic matter through dipole alignment and surface binding affinities. Density functional theory calculations and electrochemical analyses demonstrate that interfacial H2O reorientation serves as a pivotal gating step, promoting inner-sphere electron transfer between peracetic acid and target contaminants. The quantum probability density microkinetic model was developed to elucidate the crucial role of interfacial water orientation and HB restructuring frequency in mitigating mass-transfer limitations. Furthermore, the DIOP continuous-flow device achieves a 100% micropollutant removal over 180 h with minimal metal leaching. This work elucidates the role of interfacial H2O dynamics in heterogeneous oxidation, offering a generalizable design strategy for advanced wastewater purification.

articles.title:
Gas Chromatography-High
Resolution Mass Spectrometry
Spatiotemporal Screening of River Rhine Suspended Particulate Matter
(2005–2022): An Early-Warning Tool for Contaminants of Concern
articles.abstract: Abstract Environmental monitoring of archived suspended particulate matter (SPM) provides a basis for retrospective assessment of emerging contaminants in river systems. This study used yearly resolved SPM samples from two sites in the River Rhine, Koblenz and Weil am Rhein, to generate and prioritize gas chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry (GC-HRMS) data within an early warning system (EWS). The aim was to identify potential contaminants of emerging concern (CEC) showing increasing temporal trends. Of ∼3300 blank-filtered and aligned features, ∼400 exhibited significant trends (p < 0.05), of which ∼80 showed increasing trends. Tentative annotation was performed using spectral libraries which tentatively identified 234 compounds. Cross-referencing tentatively identified compounds showing increasing trends with ECOSAR-modeled aquatic toxicity identified 12 compounds with significant increasing trends and high predicted aquatic toxicity (ρ > 0.6, LC50/EC50 < 1 mg/L). Among the compounds prioritized, tentatively annotated α-methylstyrene oligomers and linear siloxanes accounted for four and three compounds, respectively, indicating recurrent compound-group signals warranting further investigation into their identities, potential co-occurring isomers, concentrations, sources, and subsequently associated risks. Although tentative identification remained a limitation of the GC-HRMS workflow, which relied on hard ionization, these results demonstrate the value of sample archives for temporally resolved prioritization in HRMS-based EWS approaches and highlight their potential for identifying potential CEC.

articles.title:
Wildfire-Driven
Release of Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals
from Tree Biomass
articles.abstract: Abstract Fire-prone regions and longer fire seasons are projected to increase with climate warming, intensifying forest disturbance. Many persistent endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs), including polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), can bioaccumulate in forest biomass through long-range atmospheric transport and local deposition, effectively turning forests into contaminant reservoirs. In this Perspective, we expand the concept of wildfire as a driver of remobilization of sequestered EDCs and argue that wildfire can shift forests from sinks to episodic sources of EDC emissions and runoff. We synthesize evidence that EDCs accumulate in tree tissues globally and outline how wildfire may remobilize biomass-sequestered EDCs through coupled atmospheric, terrestrial, and aquatic pathways. Using PFAS as a representative class, we introduce a screening-level model of pre-existing PFAS mass mobilized from burned aboveground wooded biomass. For Greece's 2023 fire season (127,602 ha), a weighted tissue concentration of ∼137.2 ng·g–1 yields a theoretical maximum release of ∼1.22 metric tons (9.6 g·ha–1). Finally, we propose physicochemical criteria to identify EDCs susceptible to wildfire-mediated release and highlight priority research directions to quantify cross-media fluxes in the era of persistent chemical production.

articles.title:
Field Aging of Biochar
Drives SOC Accumulation by
Promoting Photosynthetic Carbon Input and Shifting Soil Microbial
Communities
articles.abstract: Abstract Biochar application is an effective strategy for enhancing the soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. However, the extent to which biochar aging affects the SOC sequestration remains unclear. In this study, we investigated SOC dynamics, photosynthetic carbon allocation patterns, and soil microbial characteristics across a 1- to 5-year biochar aging gradient in a wheat farmland. The results revealed that the SOC content increased by 20.7% after 1 year of biochar application, primarily because of an increase in particulate organic carbon (POC), and increased by an additional 14.8% over the next 4 years, which resulted from additional increases in both POC and mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC). The total 13C assimilation increased by 19.9% and 33.0% after 1 and 5 years of biochar application, respectively. Moreover, biochar application promoted the accumulation of 13C in POC, while 5 years of biochar application also increased the assimilated 13C in MAOC. Furthermore, biochar aging altered the soil bacterial community and increased the abundance of saprotrophic fungi, which were strongly related to SOC dynamics. In summary, our results indicate that biochar aging promotes SOC sequestration by promoting photosynthetic carbon assimilation and facilitating the transformation of plant-derived carbon into SOC related to shifts in the soil microbial community.

articles.title:
Drivers of Regional
Aerosol pH Differences over Eastern
China Quantified with a Thermodynamic Framework
articles.abstract: Abstract Aerosol pH governs atmospheric multiphase chemistry, yet quantifying its regional drivers consistently across meteorologically and chemically diverse regions within a single thermodynamically accurate framework remains challenging. Here, we couple the regional chemical transport model Weather Research and Forecasting-Goddard Earth Observing System with Chemistry (WRF-GC) with the Extended Aerosol Inorganics Model (E-AIM) to compute wintertime aerosol pH over six key target regions of eastern China, decompose the drivers of regional pH differences and intramonthly variability through an ammonia gas-particle partitioning framework, and extend this framework to a scenario-response analysis. Monthly mean pH ranges from 2.54 to 4.32, more acidic in the south and more alkaline at higher latitudes. Temperature is the leading driver of the regional pH deviation in the YRD, PRD, and NEP (contributing 58%–63%), whereas in the high-emission NCP and FWP the deviation is instead dominated by NH3 (41%–58%). Negative covariance among the drivers substantially damps intramonthly pH fluctuations, consistent with multiphase buffering. The sensitivity of pH to ammonia reduction rises sharply as aerosols approach an ammonia-poor regime, such that large emission reductions of ammonia would decrease wintertime aerosol pH well beyond linear expectations, with pronounced inter-regional differences. By resolving these drivers on benchmark-level thermodynamics, these results provide a quantitative, region-specific basis for anticipating how aerosol pH responds to differentiated emission-reduction strategies.

articles.title:
Quantifying the
Vehicle Emission Reduction Required
to Offset Warming-Driven Ozone Increase in Beijing
articles.abstract: Abstract Vehicle emissions (VE) reductions are a key pathway for mitigating urban ozone pollution, but their effectiveness under the condition of warming-driven biogenic emission responses remains unclear. An ozone formation path tracing (OFPT) method coupling an observation-based model (OBM) with Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) was used to quantify the contribution of different VOCs for different emission sources to the ozone production rate (PO3). In this study, initial VOC concentrations were reconstructed by correcting for photochemical losses, and an additional constraint on isoprene was applied to improve the assessment of ozone production in Beijing. The results show that initial VOC reconstruction substantially increased PO3 and changed source attribution. Biogenic emissions became the largest single contributor to PO3, whereas VE remained the dominant controllable anthropogenic source because it supplied both VOCs and NOx. After considering the temperature response of isoprene emissions, a 10.7 ± 3.5% reduction in VE was required to offset the O3 increase caused by a 1 °C temperature rise under current conditions. Future-scenario simulations showed that the required VE reductions were lower under the Clean Air scenario (7.1 ± 0.7%) than under the Baseline scenario (11.3 ± 0.1%). These results highlight the need to integrate vehicle electrification, biogenic VOC responses, and warming effects into future ozone control strategies.

articles.title:
Depth-Dependent
eDNA Abundances across Ecosystems
Inform Deep-Sea Sampling Strategies
articles.abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) surveys are increasingly used to assess marine biodiversity and inform deep-sea environmental decision-making, including mineral resource management and fisheries oversight. Yet standard low-volume protocols inherited from coastal work may be inadequate at depth, and recent findings indicate that depth- and productivity-aware sampling, often requiring high-volume in situ filtration, is needed. Currently no quantitative framework links depth and ecosystem context to define defensible filtration volume targets. We compiled 841 eDNA samples from eight expeditions across the North Atlantic, Wider Caribbean Region, and Pacific (surface to 4000 m) to quantify how recoverable eDNA scales with depth and surface productivity, and to derive depth- and productivity-aware sampling targets. Total eDNA concentration declined with depth as a power law, with attenuation exponents (b) modulated by surface productivity: most gradual in eutrophic waters (b = 0.67), intermediate in mesotrophic (b = 0.90), and steepest in oligotrophic systems (b = 1.25). Volume-weighted models explained 66–88% of the variance. At a fixed extract-concentration target, required filtration volumes diverged ∼7-fold between oligotrophic and eutrophic systems at 200 m and ∼38-fold at 4000 m. Conventional Niskin sampling therefore undersamples deep-sea animal eDNA, particularly in mid- to low-productivity systems. Among laboratory parameters, the assay-specific extract-concentration target exerted greater leverage on required volume than extraction efficiency or elution volume. Volume-aware sampling paired with optimized recovery should be routine in deep-sea eDNA surveys.

articles.title:
Tire-Derived
Chemicals in Human Populations: A Global
Review of Exposure Pathways, Biomonitoring Evidence, Health Outcomes,
and Risk Assessment Implications
articles.abstract: Abstract Tire wear generates diverse tire-derived chemicals (TDCs), including antioxidants, accelerators, and their transformation products, yet human internal exposure remains poorly characterized. This review provides the first systematic synthesis of global biomonitoring evidence for TDCs in human populations, integrating exposure pathways, biological barrier penetration, and preliminary epidemiological findings. Biomonitoring data spanning four continents reveal widespread detection of multiple TDC classes such as p-phenylenediamines (PPDs), p-phenylenediamine quinones (PPD-Qs), benzothiazoles (BTHs), and benzotriazoles (BTRs), in urine and blood, with urinary concentrations consistently exceeding blood levels. Compound-specific patterns, including the predominance of 6PPD-Q over its parent compound 6PPD and substantial contributions from additional congeners (e.g., DPPD-Q, IPPD-Q, 1-OH-BTR), indicate that single-compound biomarkers are insufficient for capturing overall TDC exposure. TDCs have been detected in cord blood, amniotic fluid, cerebrospinal fluid, breast milk, and semen, documenting occurrence across multiple biological compartments and potential exposure during critical developmental windows. Preliminary epidemiological associations link TDC exposure to adverse birth outcomes, neurodevelopmental effects, and carcinogenic risks, though evidence remains constrained by limited sample sizes and narrow geographic representation: China-based studies dominate the literature, while regions with extensive environmental TDC monitoring (e.g., Europe, North America) largely lack corresponding human data, a mismatch that hinders exposure pathway attribution. Collectively, these findings indicate that TDCs represent a ubiquitous but underrecognized human exposure, and we outline priority considerations for risk assessment, including vulnerable population protection, congener-specific mixture effects, analytical standardization, and interim biomonitoring reference values.

articles.title:
Source
Attribution,
Driving Force Interpretation,
and Nature-Based Mitigation of Anthropogenic Water Pollution
articles.abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic pollution induced by combined sewer overflow (CSO) threatens urban aquatic ecosystems, yet the source contributions and driving mechanisms of its pollutants from surface runoff and domestic wastewater remain unclear. Here, we propose an analytical framework coupling high-resolution water quality modeling with climatic and socioeconomic (SSP-RCP) projections to characterize spatiotemporal dynamics and source contributions of CSO pollution under changing environments. Random Forest (RF) with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed to identify critical drivers of each source. Lorenz curves and Gini coefficient were introduced to evaluate nature-based solutions (NbS) against extreme CSOs. Application of the framework in a typical urban area demonstrated the dominant contribution of runoff pollution (78–88%) to annual loads of 2500–4200 tons, with uncertainty bounds (UB) of 2300–5800 tons. RF-SHAP analysis revealed nonlinear pollution exacerbation around transition points of approximately 8 days for dry-weather period, 0.45 for surface imperviousness, and 2000 inhabitants/km2 for population density. NbS practices mitigated 19–77% of runoff pollution and 52–76% of domestic pollution, decreasing Gini coefficients from 0.69 to 0.49 (UB: 0.40–0.82). The findings provide quantitative support for compliance with the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive, offering a replicable reference for pollution attribution, driver identification, and mitigation assessment under changing environments.

articles.title: Dual Pathways of Fe2+ Uptake Drive Intracellular Fenton Chemistry and Ferroptosis-like Cell Death of Escherichia coli upon Exposure to Reduced Nontronite
articles.abstract: Abstract Reduced iron-containing clay (RIC) minerals display strong antibacterial activity, yet the intracellular processes underlying bacterial cell death remain poorly understood. Herein, Escherichia coli knockout strains were exposed to a model RIC mineral, reduced nontronite (rNAu-2), to dissect iron influx pathways and the resulting oxidative damage. Two complementary mechanisms of Fe2+ influx were identified: (i) active transport through FeoB proteins and (ii) passive permeation across oxidatively compromised membranes. At low rNAu-2 loading, a feoB mutant accumulated less labile Fe and survived better than the E. coli wild-type (WT), whereas at higher loading, passive permeation dominated and the genotypic differences diminished. Intracellular radical analysis revealed hydroxyl radicals (•OH) as the predominant cytotoxic species. Deleting superoxide dismutases (sodA or sodC) improved bacterial survival by limiting H2O2 availability, whereas loss of peroxidase (ahpC) or catalase (katG) activity elevated H2O2 and •OH production, and heightened cellular vulnerability. rNAu-2 exposure promoted lipid peroxidation and malondialdehyde accumulation, while increasing reliance on glutathione biosynthesis (gshA), indicative of ferroptosis-like cell death. Correspondingly, a recombination-deficient mutant (recA) was hypersensitive to rNAu-2, underscoring the role of oxidative DNA damage in bacterial cell death. These results elucidate the molecular mechanisms of RIC-mediated bacterial killing and significantly advance the current model of antibacterial clay activity.

articles.title:
Meta
Life Cycle Assessment, Techno-Economic Analysis,
and Risk Assessment of Carbon Mineralization Pathways to Inform Policy
Frameworks
articles.abstract: Abstract Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even though carbon capture is already factored into all major global climate models, with mineralization (converting CO2 into stable carbonates) representing a major subset. If mineralization is to bolster the suite of climate mitigation strategies, it is vital that academic guidance be provided to inform the currently underinformed policy direction. To address this, this study presents a meta life cycle and techno-economic analysis of carbon mineralization pathways from both academia and industry, normalizing independent techno-economic, life cycle, and risk assessment (Monte Carlo) results within the context of US and EU policy. Results demonstrate that in situ mineralization achieves the greatest life cycle GHG emission reductions at the lowest cost and is the only pathway capable of gigaton-scale emission reductions commensurate with climate goals. Enhanced rock weathering also consistently delivers net-negative GHG removal at relatively low costs, but ex situ pathways achieve lower GHG emission reductions at higher costs, where several proposed pathways are net-CO2 positive as CO2 emitted throughout the process (transportation, electricity use, and natural gas combustion) offsets CO2 sequestered. Risks of leakage, hazards, global capacity, financial impact, and reversal are also quantitatively and qualitatively compared among the mineralization pathways, demonstrating that in situ mineralization has low financial risk when bolstered by state entities, faces uncertainties in non-governmental organization objection, and, ultimately, all pathways are victims of uncharted policy.
